jd.job_title: High-Speed IO Architect - Digital - PCIe/UCIe/Ethernet Subsystems
required_skills: 5+ years at Principal level or higher in fabless or IDM semiconductor
Deep PCIe architecture expertise (PHY layer through controller and protocol stack)
UCIe standard familiarity (flit-based transport, sideband protocol, die-to-die integration)
Signal integrity expertise (S-parameter analysis, HSPICE/IBIS-AMI, eye diagram closure, crosstalk budgeting)
Experience with advanced nodes and advanced packaging (CoWoS, EMIB, InFO)
Track record driving complex multi-party IP integrations from architecture through tape-out
preferred_skills: 224G/400G+ SerDes architectures for scale-up AI fabric (NVLink, UALink, Ultra Ethernet, proprietary)
Electrical-optical co-design for CPO or near-package optics
EIC retimer or photonic interface experience
Chiplet-based multi-die architectures (bumping strategy, KGD handling, heterogeneous integration)
PCIe-SIG membership or active UCIe Consortium contribution
Prior startup experience or comfort with early-stage ambiguity
key_responsibilities: Define high-speed IO architecture for PCIe/Ethernet-224G/448G scale-up fabric/CPO-optics interfaces
Define die-to-die interface architecture for UCIe integration (flit formats, credit-based flow control, sideband management)
Architect SerDes-to-photonics interface and co-packaged optics (CPO) readiness
Own signal integrity budget (TX/RX equalization, channel loss allocation, crosstalk margins, jitter decomposition)
Guide SerDes PHY selection and IP evaluation
Define and review UCIe PHY integration (bump map, power domains, analog/digital co-design, pad ring)
Collaborate on protocol bridge design (PCIe TLP ↔ UCIe flit conversion)
Drive DFT and compliance test architecture for PCIe certification and UCIe conformance
Establish PVT margin strategies and power management
Serve as primary technical interface to anchor customers and hyperscalers (AWS, Google, Microsoft, Meta)
Contribute to RTL reuse strategy for derivative SKUs
Identify and scope patentable innovations in UCIe integration and adaptive equalization
